project.name: silversea
project.description: Silversea (TingTing) business-domain knowledge graph: maps the platform's core domains (Trip Operations, Finance & Billing, Advances & Governance, Salary & Payroll, Forwarder & Customer Portal, Fleet & Master Data), their business flows, and ordered process steps to the implementing code.

nodes.name: Trip Operations
nodes.summary: Core container-trip lifecycle: a trip is created, dispatched to a driver, transitions through in-transit and completed, then locked for settlement. Covers trip commands, the status state machine, trip pairing, container/photo capture, and GPS geotag capture.

businessRules: Trip status transitions: CREATED -> IN_TRANSIT -> COMPLETED -> LOCKED (or CANCELED) are enforced by the status machine service.
A locked trip is immutable to settlement — unlocks require governance approval and post a reversal ledger entry.
Trip pairing links two legs (import/export) into a round trip for salary and profitability.
crossDomainInteractions: Posts revenue and cost to Finance-Billing ledger

nodes.name: Finance & Billing
nodes.summary: The financial engine: ledger transaction posting, customer statements, debit-note and billing-document assembly, payment application and allocation, penalties, profit distribution, and AR/AP aging. All money flows through round2dp and the shared calculations.

businessRules: Every money movement posts a LedgerEntry with a TxnType; debits and credits must balance per document.
Billing documents are assembled from trip revenue, fuel, penalties, and ancillary charges via billing-line-assembly, guarded against overlaps.
Profit distribution is gated by governance approval before disbursement.
crossDomainInteractions: Feeds receivables aging to customer statements in Forwarder-Customer-Portal
Disbursements flow to Advances-Governance and Salary-Payroll

nodes.name: Advances & Governance
nodes.summary: The approval-authority layer: forwarder advance requests and their settlement lifecycle (PENDING -> CHECKED_BY_ACCOUNTANT -> APPROVED/REJECTED -> REVERSED), the governance-action queue for financial adjustments, credit-limit overrides, and debt offsets. This is where MANAGER/DIRECTOR sign-off happens.

businessRules: Credit overrides are tiered: FINANCE_TIER_1 vs DIRECTOR approval based on scope and amount.
Advance settlements require accountant check before manager approval; reversals re-open the advance.
crossDomainInteractions: Authorizes credit-limit exceptions exposed in Forwarder-Customer-Portal

nodes.name: Salary & Payroll
nodes.summary: Driver compensation: attendance tracking, commission calculation, payslip assembly, and salary-period processing. Computes driver salary from paired trips, attendance status (TRIP_DAY/STANDBY/PERSONAL_LEAVE/WEEKLY_OFF), and incidental costs, using shared salary calculations.

businessRules: Salary is computed per salary period from paired trips and attendance; exclusions are explicit and governed.
Commission is layered on base salary per the commission service; payslips are confirmed via salary-confirmation governance.
crossDomainInteractions: Consumes paired trip data from Trip-Operations
Salary payouts post to Finance-Billing ledger as DRIVER_SALARY/DRIVER_PAYOUT

nodes.name: Forwarder & Customer Portal
nodes.summary: The role-scoped external surfaces: forwarders manage shipments, containers, and delivery confirmations; customers view their shipments, download statements and debit-note PDFs, and see receivables — all scoped per-customer/business-unit. The multi-tenant boundary of the platform.

businessRules: Every portal query is scoped by customer link or business unit — a forwarder/customer never sees another tenant's data.
Debit-note PDFs and statements are generated per-customer from the billing and statement services.
crossDomainInteractions: Reads receivables and documents from Finance-Billing

nodes.name: Fleet & Master Data
nodes.summary: The configuration backbone: drivers, trucks, trailers, tires (with position tracking), routes, cargo types, pricing tables, fuel config and norms, penalty reasons, and the business calendar. Master data that the operational and financial domains depend on.

businessRules: Pricing tables and fuel norms drive trip cost/revenue calculations; changes are governed for pricing.
Tire lifecycle is tracked per position across trucks and trailers.
The business calendar defines working days, weekly offs, and holidays used by attendance and salary.
crossDomainInteractions: Drivers/trucks are referenced by every operational flow

nodes.name: Trip Lifecycle
nodes.summary: The full journey of a container trip from creation to lock: create, dispatch, transit, complete, then lock for settlement. Each transition is guarded by the status machine and audit-logged.

nodes.name: create
nodes.summary: Create a new trip (CREATED) with route, driver, truck/trailer, cargo, and pricing — validated by shared Zod schemas.

nodes.name: dispatch
nodes.summary: Dispatch the trip to a driver; transition CREATED -> IN_TRANSIT and capture the dispatch handoff.

nodes.name: in-transit
nodes.summary: Track the trip in transit; capture GPS geotag and ETA from the GPS provider integration.

nodes.name: complete
nodes.summary: Mark the trip COMPLETED; finalize containers and delivery confirmation via the forwarder.

nodes.name: lock
nodes.summary: Lock the completed trip (LOCKED) for settlement; post revenue and cost to the ledger. Unlocks require governance approval.

nodes.name: Trip Pairing
nodes.summary: Pair an import trip with an export trip into a round trip so driver salary and profitability are computed on the combined journey.

nodes.name: select-legs
nodes.summary: Select two compatible trip legs (e.g. import + export) for pairing based on route and driver.

nodes.name: validate
nodes.summary: Validate pairing constraints (same driver, contiguous routes, timing) before committing.

nodes.name: commit
nodes.summary: Create the TripPair record linking the legs; downstream salary and profitability use the pair.

nodes.name: Billing Document Assembly
nodes.summary: Assemble a customer billing document from trip revenue, fuel, penalties, and ancillary charges, then guard against overlapping billing and generate the debit-note PDF.

nodes.name: gather-lines
nodes.summary: Gather billable lines (trip revenue, fuel cost, penalties, ancillary revenue) for the period and customer.

nodes.name: guard-overlap
nodes.summary: Guard against overlapping billing — ensure no trip is double-billed across documents.

nodes.name: assemble
nodes.summary: Assemble the billing document rows and compute totals via shared calculations.

nodes.name: debit-note
nodes.summary: Transition the debit-note status and render the templated debit-note PDF/XLSX.

nodes.name: Payment Application & Allocation
nodes.summary: Receive a customer or vendor payment, allocate it against outstanding receivables/payables using FIFO aging, and post the ledger entry.

nodes.name: receive
nodes.summary: Receive the payment via the idempotent payments route; validate the idempotency key.

nodes.name: allocate
nodes.summary: Allocate the payment against outstanding documents using FIFO aging prioritization.

nodes.name: post-ledger
nodes.summary: Post the PAYMENT_RECEIVED ledger entry and update AR status; trigger receivable-reminder cancellation if settled.

nodes.name: Advance Settlement
nodes.summary: The advance settlement lifecycle: a forwarder advance is requested, checked by an accountant, approved/rejected by a manager, then optionally reversed.

nodes.name: request
nodes.summary: Forwarder submits an advance request (PENDING) against expected trip earnings.

nodes.name: accountant-check
nodes.summary: Accountant checks the settlement (PENDING -> CHECKED_BY_ACCOUNTANT), verifying evidence and amounts.

nodes.name: manager-approve
nodes.summary: Manager approves or rejects; on approval, funds disburse and a FORWARDER_ADVANCE ledger entry posts.

nodes.name: reversal
nodes.summary: Optional reversal reopens the settlement and posts a reversal entry if it was wrongly approved.

nodes.name: Governance Action Queue
nodes.summary: The authority queue for financial adjustments, credit-limit overrides, and debt offsets: submit -> check -> approve/reject/return-for-evidence, with tiered approval (FINANCE_TIER_1 vs DIRECTOR).

nodes.name: submit
nodes.summary: Submit a governance action (adjustment, credit override, or debt offset) into the queue (PENDING).

nodes.name: check
nodes.summary: Validate the action against governance policy and the tier rules; route to the correct authority tier.

nodes.name: decide
nodes.summary: Authority approves, rejects, or returns-for-evidence; the decision is audit-logged and posts/effects the underlying ledger entry.

nodes.name: Salary Period Close
nodes.summary: Close a salary period: gather attendance and paired trips, compute base salary + commission, assemble payslips, confirm via governance, and disburse.

nodes.name: gather-attendance
nodes.summary: Gather driver attendance records (TRIP_DAY/STANDBY/PERSONAL_LEAVE/WEEKLY_OFF) for the period from the business calendar.

nodes.name: compute-salary
nodes.summary: Compute base salary from paired trips and incidental costs via the shared tripDriverSalary calculation.

nodes.name: compute-commission
nodes.summary: Layer commission onto the base salary per the commission service.

nodes.name: confirm
nodes.summary: Confirm payslips via salary-confirmation governance before disbursement.

nodes.name: disburse
nodes.summary: Disburse payouts, posting DRIVER_SALARY/DRIVER_PAYOUT ledger entries.

nodes.name: Customer Statement
nodes.summary: Generate a customer receivables statement: assemble outstanding documents, compute aging, and export as PDF or XLSX for the customer portal.

nodes.name: scope
nodes.summary: Scope the query to the logged-in customer via user-customer links and business units.

nodes.name: assemble
nodes.summary: Assemble statement data from the ledger and billing documents, computing FIFO aging buckets.

nodes.name: export
nodes.summary: Export the statement as PDF (or XLSX) and stream it to the customer.

nodes.name: Pricing Table Governance
nodes.summary: Governed changes to pricing tables and fuel norms: propose, validate against the price-config governance, approve, and apply — since pricing directly drives all billing.

nodes.name: propose
nodes.summary: Propose a pricing-table or fuel-norm change through the governed config route.

nodes.name: validate
nodes.summary: Validate the proposal against price-config governance rules before it can take effect.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Apply the approved pricing; downstream trip cost/revenue calculations pick up the new values.

edges.description: Trips post revenue and fuel/driver cost to the ledger on lock; billing documents assemble trip revenue.
Paired trips and attendance feed driver salary computation.
Financial adjustments, profit distribution, and disbursements are gated by the governance-action queue.
Receivables and billing documents back customer statements and debit-note PDFs in the portal.
Credit-limit overrides authorize shipment creation beyond a customer's standard limit.
Pricing tables, fuel norms, routes, and the driver/truck roster are referenced by every trip.
The business calendar and driver master data drive attendance and salary.
